heading_path.h3: Worked example 4.7: Converting common fractions to decimal fractions

records.raw_html:
Worked example 4.7: Converting common fractions to decimal fractions

Write as a decimal fraction.

  1. Step 1: Divide the denominator into the numerator. If it cannot divide, write a zero.

  2. Step 2: Put a decimal point after the zero and after the numerator.

  3. Step 3: Add zeros after the decimal point in the numerator.

    The numbers 5; 5.0; 5.00; 5.000; 5.0000 and so on all represent the value 5.

  4. Step 4: Carry on with the division.

  5. Step 5: Write down the answer.

    The division will carry on forever, because we keep on getting the same remainder. This is called a recurring decimal. We write it with a dot above the digit that repeats.
records.answer_text:
Step 1: Divide the denominator into the numerator. If it cannot divide, write a zero.

$$
\require{enclose}
\begin{array}{r}
0\\
6 \enclose{longdiv}{5}\\
\end{array}
$$

Step 2: Put a decimal point after the zero and after the numerator.

$$
\require{enclose}
\begin{array}{r}
0.\\
6 \enclose{longdiv}{5.}\\
\end{array}
$$

Step 3: Add zeros after the decimal point in the numerator.

$$
\require{enclose}
\begin{array}{r}
0.\phantom{0000}\\
6 \enclose{longdiv}{5.0000}\\
\end{array}
$$

The numbers 5; 5.0; 5.00; 5.000; 5.0000 and so on all represent the value 5.

Step 4: Carry on with the division.

$$
\require{enclose}
\begin{array}{l}
\phantom{00} 0.8\,3\,3\, ...\\
6 \enclose{longdiv}{5.0\,0\,0\,0}\\
\,\underline{-0}\downarrow\,\downarrow\,\downarrow \,\downarrow \\
\phantom{00} 5\,0 \\
\,\underline{-4\,8} \\
\,\phantom{000} 2\,0  \\
\phantom{00}\underline{-1\,8} \\
\phantom{00000} 2\,0   \\
\;\phantom{000}\underline{-1\,8}  \\
\;\phantom{000000} 2\,0   \\
\end{array}
$$

Step 5: Write down the answer.

The division will carry on forever, because we keep on getting the same remainder. This is called a recurring decimal. We write it with a dot above the digit that repeats.

$$
\therefore \frac{5}{6}=0.8\dot{3}
$$

records.raw_html: As well as writing a fraction as a common fraction or a decimal fraction, we may also express a fraction as a percentage. A percentage is a fraction in which the denominator is always 100. Only the numerator is written down, followed by a percentage symbol: %. The symbol shows that the number we wrote down gives the parts of a whole that is divided into 100.
